recentItems.description:
Trump's Party On Major Reshuffle Path? All Eyes On Rubio, Vance, Hegseth After Midterm Loss  

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports suggesting he is considering leaving Donald Trump's administration to prepare for a potential 2028 presidential run. In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio said working for Trump until the end of his term has always been his plan and reiterated his commitment to his current role.

recentItems.title: Punjab PCS Results Rocked By Rigging Claims; TN Hit By Horse-Trading Row | Setting The Agenda
recentItems.description:
Punjab's PCS Mains results trigger a political storm as the BJP alleges large-scale irregularities and questions the selection process, while the AAP government rejects the charges. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court raises concerns over Delhi's worsening air pollution, stubble burning and vehicular emissions. In Tamil Nadu, allegations of horse-trading intensify after the arrest of former Madurai Deputy Mayor PM Mannan over claims of attempts to poach TVK MLAs.

recentItems.title: Big 'NO' To Putin For G20 Entry, UK's Andy Burnham GOES Tough, RIDICULES RUSSIAN President
recentItems.description:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out inviting Russian President Vladimir Putin to the 2027 G20 summit in Manchester, delivering a blunt "No" when asked about his participation. The decision marks a tough stance against Moscow and could deepen diplomatic tensions between Russia and Western nations.

recentItems.title: Ghalibaf's Sharp Dig As Vance Blames Trump's Iran War After Republicans' Face Loss In Midterm Rout
recentItems.description:
Ghalibaf's Sharp Dig As Vance Blames Trump's Iran War After Republicans' Face Loss In Midterm Rout

Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has mocked US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance following the Republican Party's major losses in the November 3 midterm elections. The political jibe came after Vance acknowledged that the ongoing US-Iran war had contributed to the GOP's electoral defeat, with some Trump supporters reportedly shifting towards the Democrats over dissatisfaction with the conflict.
